methods.gap: DINO FG/BG margin near zero because similar semantic distractor dominates. Target and distractor have distinct reference-conditioned RGB, but a global photometric shift invalidates direct RGB transfer.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Use reference BG and DINO-confident query BG only to estimate per-channel median location/scale nuisance; unlike DINO whitening, RGB nuisance fit is explicit diagonal affine and does not remove DINO semantic variance. The correction is useful only if BG-anchor mixture remains comparable. Synthetic first check found the aligned nearest-median control solved the witness equally; primary was simplified to that control rather than attributing the alignment gain to complex density.
algorithm: Build the direct DINO FG–BG prototype margin m and downsample true RGB to its aligned grid.
Estimate per-channel medians/MAD in known R BG and Q tokens with m<=−0.25; fewer than 8 anchors => no alignment.
Map Q RGB by the diagonal affine median/MAD map, with scale clipped to [0.5,2]; fixed floor 1/255.
Fit weighted known R FG/BG RGB medians; primary uses aligned nearest-median squared distance, preserving the minimal successful observation.
h=(dB−dF)/(dF+dB), 0/0=>0. Product Laplace likelihood is a stronger same-input control, not the source of claimed gain.
Primary complete margin m+0.5*h; produce full mask by fixed readout.
Controls: m alone, unaligned RGB likelihood, aligned nearest RGB prototype, RGB-only likelihood with identical readout.
methods.expected_benefit: synthetic hypothesis: correct a color-distinct distractor rejection despite an affine RGB illumination shift, when BG anchor composition is genuinely stable.
methods.simplest_control: Unaligned/ aligned two RGB medians with the identical DINO cap; BG-anchor oracle is forbidden.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Prior RGB Potts uses only Q edge contrasts; this decision uses known R RGB FG/BG class likelihood plus explicitly limited photometric normalization. Distinct from DINO covariance whitening.
methods.counterexample: Q background is a different scene color or DINO confident BG contains target: nuisance map is not illumination and can invert identity; target changes color across instances.
methods.first_evidence: Witness where Q target/distractor DINO margins tie but known-background anchors have m<=−0.25, R RGB classes separate and Q undergoes a shared-channel affine illumination transform; negative: absent anchors, different BG composition and FG/BG RGB appearance swap. Compare all simple controls.
methods.failure_reflection: If aligned prototype ties primary, retain the simpler control; if nuisance harms while unaligned wins, background composition/seed contamination rather than lack of color evidence is diagnosed.
methods.revision_note: Same mechanism/inputs, reduced classifier complexity after same-information control; no new method count.

methods.title: 参考监督的局部序纹理直方图
methods.gap: DINO and RGB color histograms tie when objects share colors but differ in local brightness ordering.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: For each 16x16 true RGB gray patch, 8-neighbor rank comparisons encode local ordinal structure. Positive affine intensity transformations preserve comparisons. This differs from radial power shares; whether it adds beyond power must be tested.
algorithm: Compute direct DINO margin m; obtain aligned 16x16 RGB gray windows for all R/Q token centers.
For each inner pixel compute 8-neighbor >= center binary code; collapse each code to minimum cyclic rotation.
Form normalized histogram over all 36 rotation-equivalence codes per patch.
Use only pure known R FG/BG windows; fewer than 4 each => abstain.
Build weighted mean FG/BG histograms; h=(dB−dF)/(dF+dB) using Hellinger squared distances.
Primary m+0.5*h with complete fixed mask output.
Controls: DINO only, identical-window color histogram, gray variance, radial-power histogram, dominant-band descriptor.
methods.expected_benefit: synthetic hypothesis: local-order identity evidence when patch colors and radial power are insufficient, without assuming target location/size.
methods.simplest_control: Same-window dominant frequency/energy and radial power, not only an intentionally weak global color histogram.
methods.why_not_duplicate: RGB local ordinal order is not query color-path propagation or existing radial Fourier power. If no witness beats existing power controls, reviewer should reject as unsupported texture variant.
methods.counterexample: DINO-target and non-target have same local ordinal texture, or texture scale is changed/blurred in Q; repeated ordinal texture on background causes coherent FP.
methods.first_evidence: Seek one deterministic same-color/power-tied local-order witness and preserve a matched texture wrong-category negative. No synthetic success => remain unverified, not counted as positive.
methods.failure_reflection: A win over color but tie/loss to power means local order is unnecessary on that setting; domain texture change separates transfer failure from implementation error.

methods.title: 参考监督的三频相位耦合
methods.gap: Power descriptors cannot distinguish patches with equal Fourier amplitude but different higher-order phase organization; DINO/color may also tie.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Normalized bispectral products X(k)X(l)conj(X(k+l)) preserve translation phase cancellation and observe phase relationships erased by power. This is a precise new observable; translation on cyclic patch is the exact invariance, not arbitrary natural-image scale invariance.
algorithm: Compute m and true RGB gray 16x16 windows, subtract per-window mean.
Normalize each triple by product of amplitudes with zero-amplitude result 0; concatenate real/imag parts.
Average descriptors over 4 discrete 90-degree patch rotations; no arbitrary-angle invariance claim.
Only pure R FG/BG windows fit mean descriptors; missing or equal means => abstain.
h=(dB−dF)/(dF+dB) from squared distance; primary m+0.5*h and complete mask.
Controls: same-window full 2D power nearest-prototype, existing radial/peak power, local ordinal histogram, DINO alone.
methods.expected_benefit: algebraic observer separation: equal-amplitude different-phase textures may become distinguishable. Natural RGB gains remain unknown.
methods.simplest_control: Full 2D power spectrum with same reference labels and Euclidean classifier; radial-only control is not enough.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Bispectral phase relations are absent from existing radial power candidate. Distinctness requires an amplitude-identical witness and stronger power control; cannot count just another FFT ring.
methods.counterexample: Texture has unstable local phase or isotropic noise; patch translation with nonperiodic crop changes observations; identical bispectra/class textures give no identity.
methods.first_evidence: Periodic amplitude-identical FG/BG RGB fixtures with prescribed phase triples, cyclic translation check, wrong-category identical texture and scale-change negatives.
methods.failure_reflection: If phase witness works but natural input does not, diagnose cross-instance phase transfer; if ordinal histogram ties, higher-order complexity may be unnecessary even if distinct observable exists.

methods.title: 参考多模态 RGB patch 字典
methods.gap: One RGB/texture prototype averages multiple legitimate target appearances into a descriptor resembling a distractor; DINO margin is insufficient.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: A nonparametric reference dictionary retains modes and spatial pixel arrangements rather than their mean. The evidence is reference RGB patch similarity, not transfer of the reference silhouette.
algorithm: Compute m and aligned true-RGB 8x8 windows, remove each channel mean and normalize contrast; append the 3 means separately at weight 1/4.
Select at most 64 FG and 64 BG pure R windows by deterministic farthest-point sampling under patch distance; first index smallest.
At every Q window compute nearest squared patch distance to each class in blocks of 128; no Q ROI or GT selection.
Primary m+0.5*h and full mask; no template location or shape transfer.
Controls: identical RGB descriptors with one class mean, raw RGB prototype, nearest texture histogram, DINO alone.
methods.expected_benefit: synthetic hypothesis: preserve two known target appearance modes when their average coincides with background; benefit requires their actual local arrangement to repeat in Q.
methods.simplest_control: Nearest RGB patch dictionary using all allowed reference samples; class-mean same descriptor tests whether nonparametric mode retention supplies the benefit.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Existing texture computes two descriptor means after radial aggregation, not nearest labeled pixel-arrangement exemplars. This is a different decision and observation, not extra texture scales.
methods.counterexample: Viewpoint/rotation makes pixel arrangements incomparable, nearest dictionary mistakes accidental background pattern, or reference FG support is too small.
methods.first_evidence: Two FG patch modes equidistant around a BG mean, shuffled same-color negative and rotated-query transfer failure; complete query masks with m tied.
methods.failure_reflection: If RGB mean matches dictionary, multimodality hypothesis absent; if dictionary wins witness but fails RGB real inputs, patch alignment/transfer is the limitation, not evidence for DINO ceiling.

methods.title: 参考监督 DINO–RGB 邻域关系耦合
methods.gap: Separate DINO and RGB descriptors can have matching marginals for target/distractor yet pair different semantic variations with different visual variations.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Local pairwise DINO distances and local pairwise RGB distances encode their coupling. Correlation of distance matrices distinguishes matched vs mismatched co-variation, even if each modality separately has the same marginal histogram. This coupling can be measured from the given pair, not inferred from Q area.
algorithm: Build m and align physical RGB 3-channel averages to native DINO token grid.
For each 3x3 token window, compute its 36 upper-triangle cosine DINO distances and RGB squared distances.
Descriptor is centered normalized distance correlation plus RGB/DINO distance medians; constant distances => coupling zero.
Pure R FG/BG windows supervise class descriptor means; at least 4 per class or abstain.
Compute normalized distance advantage h over all Q windows.
Primary m+0.5*h and complete mask.
Controls: concatenated uncoupled DINO/RGB neighborhood distance histograms; direct DINO; permuted RGB–DINO pairing retaining all descriptor marginals.
methods.expected_benefit: algebraic hypothesis: identity can differ through cross-modal arrangement while separate marginal appearance summaries tie; real transfer unknown.
methods.simplest_control: Same pairwise distances with uncoupled concatenated histograms and pairing-permutation control. Raw RGB alone is insufficient attribution.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Neither query color smoothing nor reference Fourier power uses correspondence of DINO and RGB neighborhood changes. Distinct cross-modal dependence observer, no fixed color identity.
methods.counterexample: FG itself has weak/no RGB–DINO coupling, DINO context couples shadows instead of class, or class and distractor have identical joint relation.
methods.first_evidence: Deterministic local permutation fixtures preserving separate RGB and DINO pairwise-distance marginal distributions but changing coupling; appearance-matched wrong-class negative.
methods.failure_reflection: If uncoupled descriptors win equally, relation term unnecessary; coupling failure under Q domain change shows it is scene-dependent evidence rather than semantic identity.

methods.title: 参考监督的跨模态边界似然切分
methods.gap: Query RGB edges include internal texture/shadow edges; indiscriminate RGB Potts cannot decide which edges are target boundaries. DINO boundary and RGB boundary may jointly separate known reference cuts from internal edges.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Known R mask labels edge pairs as same-class or cut. Joint bins of relative DINO contrast and relative RGB contrast retain their dependency, unlike generic Q edge smoothing. Only positive same/cut log-likelihood becomes attractive Potts strength; identity still comes from direct DINO unary.
algorithm: Compute m and aligned R/Q DINO plus physical RGB token averages; four-neighbor edges only.

For each edge compute cosine DINO distance and RGB squared distance; quantile calibration learns their scale from reference only and uses the same bins in Q. No query-local contrast normalization is silently assumed.
Build 4x4 reference-quantile joint bins; estimate equal-prior same/cut densities with add-one counts on known pure R endpoints.
At all Q edges w=max(0,log p_same/p_cut)/4; missing R cut edges => zero pairwise.
Use identical exact binary min-cut E=-sum_i m_i*z_i + sum_e w_e*[z_a!=z_b], identical 1e6 integer capacity quantization and native signed output for all arms.
Produce full binary field and fixed output masks; no Q label/proposal inputs.

Controls: pointwise RGB-only and DINO-only reference likelihoods with the exact same unary/edges/readout/quantization. Normalize positive weights to primary total pairwise mass; if an arm has zero positive evidence use uniform weights of the same total mass; zero-edge DINO is also kept.
methods.expected_benefit: synthetic hypothesis: close a weak DINO hole while retaining true boundary when RGB-only contrasts are identical for texture and object edge but DINO/RGB dependency differs.
methods.simplest_control: Existing reference_boundary DINO-only calibrated cut and RGB Potts with identical unary, graph, readout and pairwise mass; no old pipeline mismatch.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Existing reference_boundary estimates DINO edge density alone. This uses joint DINO/RGB dependence; however decoder and reference-edge supervision are shared. Reviewer may classify as a modality extension/revision (count 0), which must be accepted.
methods.counterexample: Reference has too few pure cut edges, Q boundary appearance changes, or wrong DINO identity seeds are strengthened; boundary fitting cannot identify an entirely wrong object.
methods.first_evidence: Construct R with balanced binary DINO/RGB bits A/B, known class L=A xor B, edge transition counts n00=n11 and n01=n10. Individual edge histograms then exactly tie while joint cut/same dependency differs. A tiny label direction defines the actual DINO unary without altering double-precision edge-distance bins. Q hole/cut complete-mask witness plus exhaustive small-graph energy check; wrong-identity seed negative.
methods.failure_reflection: If joint method equals one-modality control, reject extra dependency complexity; if cut corrects holes but wrong identity grows, isolate readout benefit from identity failure.
methods.revision_note: Joint observation, not merely extra RGB weight. Comparator API and exact signed energy now match existing boundary control; same mass zero-evidence fallback explicit.

methods.title: 逐像素阴影商空间颜色判据
methods.gap: Same target albedo occurs under locally varying positive achromatic shading; RGB means move across reference class means and no global affine transform can undo the pixel-dependent nuisance.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Algebraic invariant u(s(x)*RGB)=u(RGB) for positive non-clipped scalar s(x), where u(c)=c/||c||. This removes only local brightness magnitude, preserving chromatic direction. Direct DINO identity remains the baseline.
algorithm: Validate physical uint8 RGB and complete R mask; use RGB256 recorded physical transform.
At each physical pixel form unit RGB chromatic direction; zero black pixels abstain.
Average unit chromatic directions within each native DINO cell, excluding padding.
Known R FG/BG weights fit unit class mean directions; Q h=(uQ dot uF - uQ dot uB)/2.
Output complete native margin m+0.5*h with fixed shared renderer; empty/all FG obey shared contract.
Controls: raw RGB median prototype, RGB01 global affine aligned prototype, grayscale intensity prototype, RGB-only chromaticity.
methods.expected_benefit: algebraic invariance; hypothesized recovery of chromatically distinct target under spatially varying achromatic shadow, not semantic guarantee.
methods.simplest_control: Raw and globally aligned RGB prototypes with same class support and readout; primary itself is the simple cosine RGB invariant, no elaborate log-color operator.
methods.why_not_duplicate: RGB01 estimates one global per-channel affine map from Q BG anchors; RGB07 removes a per-pixel scalar without any Q seeds. The nuisance group and decisions differ; if reviewer calls it color-feature variation, count0 accepted.
methods.counterexample: Achromatic FG/BG, colored illumination, clipped channels or same chromaticity distractor; eliminating intensity can remove class evidence.
methods.first_evidence: Spatially alternating shade multipliers per Q native cell while target and BG albedos have distinct chromaticity; negative achromatic classes where raw intensity succeeds but quotient fails.
methods.failure_reflection: Raw-only wins on achromatic class => discarded intensity carried semantics. Colored-light failure => scalar shading model broken. Do not infer general lighting invariance.

methods.available_information: Aligned frozen DINO q/r grid, reference coverage/valid weights and known producer; actual uint8 RGB images plus complete known reference mask. No Q GT, class names, external pool/model, encoder calls or remote use. Coverage-only version must be labeled separately.
methods.output_contract: Return complete field/token mask and fixed half-pixel bilinear original-size binary mask, plus exact same readout for controls. RGB observation capped as signed correction to direct FG–BG DINO prototype margin, not FoRIS score. Empty known FG => empty; all FG => full; absent or uninformative RGB observation => direct DINO control.
methods.evidence_level: hypothesized; true-data quality unknown; witness/CPU measurements pending
methods.cpu_cost: NumPy/Pillow CPU only; single BLAS thread, RGB <=256 squared, patches in blocks <=128; no N² DINO matrix, 512 MiB incremental target. Real timings must be measured, not inferred.
methods.limitations: Appearance is not semantic identity. Cross-instance color/texture changes and shared distractor appearance can violate transfer; no general gain is guaranteed.
methods.failure_accounting: Report aTP/aFP/dTP/dFP and per-class exact IoU delta only if legitimately available Q GT in a separate scorer. Without Q GT, report activity/cost and synthetic witnesses only. Wrong-seed/appearance-swap cases are negative evidence, never oracle-method proof.
methods.count_rule: Candidate only until reviewer approves distinct complete mechanism and implementation/checks; controls and parameter variations count zero.
methods.title: 参考像素 RGB 分布的混合解码
methods.gap: A native DINO patch contains a multimodal target texture and surrounding background; mean RGB and pure RGB patch templates do not identify its foreground occupancy.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Use labeled R per-pixel joint RGB histogram, then query per-pixel color evidence to fit a two-component mixture weight per native patch. This is independent RGB information, not pi inferred from the DINO score histogram. Its class-conditional color transfer assumption is explicit.
algorithm: Validate physical actual RGB and R mask; construct RGB256 in recorded transform.
Build 4x4x4 joint RGB class histograms on all known R foreground/background physical pixels with add-one smoothing and equal class priors.
For each Q native cell collect all its RGB256 pixels; let f/b be the reference class mass at each color bin.
Fit mixture alpha in [0,1] by fixed 32-iteration concave-likelihood derivative bisection; no DINO term enters estimation.
Q h=2*alpha-1; output m+0.5*h and complete mask by shared renderer.
Controls: pixel likelihood foreground fraction, mean log likelihood ratio per patch, native cell mean RGB prototype, one-step EM at alpha=.5, DINO alone.
methods.expected_benefit: hypothesized area/identity correction when color distribution identifies a true mixture and the mean collapses its modes; actual quality unknown.
methods.simplest_control: Same per-pixel FG/BG likelihoods with mean log LR or direct posterior vote; oracle alpha/true Q labels forbidden.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Existing score-derived occupancy routes never use actual R-labeled RGB pixel class distributions. RGB04 compares pure pixel-arrangement exemplars; this fits mixture prevalence without copying a template, though simpler same-information control may make it unnecessary.
methods.counterexample: Q background shares reference FG colors, unknown extra mixture component, or same-color FG/BG histograms; mixture alpha is not semantic area in those settings.
methods.first_evidence: Algebraic closure before any probe; no experiment or implementation needed.
methods.failure_reflection: The ML optimizer is a different computation of the same standalone binary decision. Confidence amplitude is a readout variation, not an independent new identity method.
methods.closure_argument: L is concave. alpha*>1/2 iff L′(1/2)>0 iff sum(f-b)/(f+b)>0 iff mean equal-prior pixel posterior>1/2, apart from nonunique/tie endpoints. Adding DINO changes only confidence magnitude; not new identity information.

history_evidence.fact: RGB Potts vs MEAN −0.027595 [−0.160435,0.032420] on reused public600; query-boundary smoothing did not establish gain.
RCG+RGB disagreement revision vs RCG +0.036362 [−0.015595,0.135117]; not stable positive.
Radial power texture already exists; its striping witness is solved by dominant-band control. It must not be recounted.

methods.title: 参考边界两侧的方向性角色判据
methods.gap: DINO identity weak and Q absolute RGB shifts from R, while the learned reference foreground-versus-local-background color contrast persists. Symmetric boundaries know only where to cut, not which side is target.
methods.new_observation_or_argument: Known reference cut edges are ordered FG to BG; their unit RGB difference direction provides a foreground-side role. Query edges can then vote toward one endpoint independently of DINO seeds. This is a learned relational contrast, not an assumed bright-target prior.
algorithm: Validate RGB/mask; obtain physical RGB means on native grids and direct DINO m.
From known pure R FG/BG four-neighbor cut edges compute ordered FG-minus-BG unit RGB difference; average and unit-normalize, zero/no cuts => abstain.
Partition Q four-neighbor grid into components joined when RGB contrast <= median R within-class RGB contrast, floor 1/255.
For inter-component Q edges, each endpoint receives signed dot(unit(c_i-c_j), reference_direction) role vote; weight by observed contrast.
Each component takes boundary-vote average and assigns it to all member tokens; no component selected by size/location.
Output m+0.5*h and complete shared-rendered mask.
Controls: pointwise absolute RGB prototype, RGB01 alignment, no-component per-edge role vote, symmetric RGB-only cut with same unary.
methods.expected_benefit: hypothesized recovery of a whole visually coherent missed region using a reference-conditioned foreground-side relation, without a correct DINO seed.
methods.simplest_control: The same learned polarity applied pointwise, plus symmetric boundary segmentation, to isolate role and component propagation; an oracle component identity is forbidden.
methods.why_not_duplicate: Query color-bottleneck inherits DINO FG/BG seeds and symmetric RGB Potts has no FG-side reference role. RGB06 fits same/cut dependency but is symmetric. This instead uses directed FG-to-BG reference contrast to supply a region identity hypothesis.
methods.counterexample: Q surrounding context reverses contrast, internal texture partitions object or merges target/background, one target borders several incompatible colors, same relational contrast distractor.
methods.first_evidence: Uniform bright-offset R/Q foreground/background with tied DINO target identity and no confident BG anchors, where absolute colors fail but ordered local contrast persists; role inversion and wrong-context negatives.
methods.failure_reflection: If pointwise role matches components, propagation unnecessary. If sign reverses under new context, a background-role transfer assumption failed; do not call the learned reference relation semantic identity guarantee.
